rows.evidence: Q1: Section 3 (Results and discussion), Figs 6-9 and Table 2 - the authors deploy their own ESP32/ThingsBoard system with DHT22, soil moisture and ultrasonic water-level sensors in a test area in Fez, Morocco, and report the readings collected (e.g. temperature 20.1-20.2 C, humidity 58.5-62%, moisture 78-80%, water level 36%) over a short time series on 28 Nov 2023.
rows.notes: The study is a system-design and demonstration paper: it shows that the IoT system can remotely monitor sensor values on a cloud dashboard, apply threshold-based pump activation, and send e-mail notifications. It never measures farmer stress, workload, wellbeing or any farmer-side outcome; no farmer survey or user evaluation is reported. It therefore only supports the precondition (remote monitoring/control and alerts exist) and not the claimed effect (reduced stress on farmers). The demonstration is a very short test run (a few minutes of readings) on one site, with no replication, no dispersion statistics beyond min/max of near-constant readings, and no stated limitations beyond a recommendation to recalibrate sensors and adapt to local conditions.

notes: Full text appears complete (sections 1-4 plus references). The paper contains no machine-learning component and no app-based scheduling per se; it is a threshold-based IoT/cloud dashboard system with e-mail alerts, which broadly matches the 'smart system with remote monitoring and control' described in the claim but offers no evidence on farmer wellbeing.
